findings.title: The telemetry boundary test asserts a key name, not the entity name, so AC-100680-04 ("no entity in telemetry") is unproven while the name is present in the very payload it inspects
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/telemetry_entity_tests.rs:122-126 serializes the recorded VerifyEvent and asserts only `!rendered.contains("\"entities\"")` — a check on the literal key `entities`. The same rendered string contains the probe name: `VerifyEvent.preview` is built by `redact_preview` (crates/clio-write/src/telemetry.rs:44, :78-94), which masks secrets only and copies the snapshot verbatim via `masked_clone` (crates/clio-write/src/telemetry.rs:83), so `preview.snapshot.entity` keeps the value. The real-binary artifact from this run's own E2E shows it on stderr: `verify {"operation":"verify_ok",...,"preview":{"diagnostic":null,"gist":"a note that mentions nothing by name","snapshot":{"amount":1,"date":"2024-01-01","entity":"Ada Lovelace"}}}` (runs/phase-100680/developer-e2e-entities.out.txt, line 3). The test therefore passes while an entity name sits in telemetry, and it would still pass if a name were added. The phase states the rule in absolute terms (phase doc:79 "entities[] ... MUST NOT enter `warnings`, `explanation`, telemetry, or health surfaces"; phase doc:244 "A boundary test proves entities are absent from `warnings`, the explain trace, telemetry, and health"), yet AC-100680-04 (phase doc:308) is marked PASS. A permanent code comment repeats the narrower truth as if it were the rule: crates/clio-write/src/telemetry.rs:16-17 "The read-side per-hit `entities[]` projection (see `clio-retrieve`), which never reaches this surface". The other three surfaces are genuinely proven: crates/clio-mcp/src/read_entities_tests.rs:213-259 (warnings + explanation sweep) and :261-278 (diagnose/verify).
findings.requirement_ref: phase 100680 §7 Required Controls / Security Acceptance Conditions (phase doc:234, :244); §2 Must Not Change (phase doc:79); AC-100680-04 (phase doc:297, :308)
findings.recommendation: Decide the rule, then make the evidence match it. Either (a) treat the absolute rule as binding and mask or drop `entity` in `redact_preview` (crates/clio-write/src/telemetry.rs:78-94), updating the pre-existing test that asserts the masked preview keeps the snapshot, and then assert the probe name is absent in telemetry_entity_tests.rs; or (b) keep the write-path preview as is and amend the phase text to scope the telemetry MUST to the read-side `entities[]` projection, rename the test to what it actually proves (e.g. `verify_telemetry_carries_no_read_side_entities_array`), assert the name where the claim is made, and reword crates/clio-write/src/telemetry.rs:16-17 so a future reader is not told telemetry is entity-free. Do not leave AC-100680-04 marked PASS on the current evidence.

findings.title: The "already span-verified" guarantee in the new docs holds only for the store-family write paths; bundle import and correct/update can store an `entity` that was never verified, and `entities[]` republishes it
findings.evidence: `verify_snapshot` has exactly three call sites, all in the verified store path: crates/clio-write/src/store_path.rs:145, :177 and crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs:149. Two production paths write a caller-supplied snapshot with no FR-4 check: the bundle import stages the restored item as-is (crates/clio-compliance/src/import_apply.rs:226 `staged.push(BatchWrite::CreateItem { item: masked_item(admitted) ... })`), and `correct_item` / `update_memory_item` take a whole `MemoryItem` from the caller (crates/clio-store/src/store.rs:53, :381; crates/clio-store/src/audit_model.rs:35-49 `pub new_item: MemoryItem`). The new documentation states the invariant without that qualification: crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs:20-22 "At write time that value had to appear as a contiguous NFC source substring, so it is the one already-verified value a read may expose", crates/clio-retrieve/src/types.rs:139-141, and docs/recall-entities.md:15 "the value that was already checked against the source text at write time". Phase doc:78 lists as Must-Not-Change "Span-verification rules (FR-4): no entity value is exposed unless it was already verified at write time", and AC-100680-01 (phase doc:305) claims sourcing "only from the verified snapshot `entity`". Mitigating fact I verified: the same authorized caller can already read the whole snapshot through `get_snapshot` (crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:128-139), so this is not a new exposure class — but the documented guarantee and the AC are broader than the code, and no Known Limitations entry covers it.
findings.requirement_ref: phase 100680 §2 Must Not Change (phase doc:78); §5 Task 1 "Only values already verified at write time are exposed" (phase doc:158); AC-100680-01 (phase doc:294, :305)
findings.recommendation: Qualify the claim to the paths that actually span-verify (`store` / `batch` / additive stores, i.e. the `gated_store_verified` family) in crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs, the `ScoredHit.entities` field doc, and docs/recall-entities.md, and add a Known Limitations entry for import-restored and corrected items. If the guarantee is meant to be absolute, the fix belongs upstream: run `verify_snapshot` (or an explicit provenance flag) on the import and correct paths before any hit can expose the value.

findings.title: Completion Evidence understates the new-test counts (says 26 total and 17 in clio-retrieve; the real numbers are 29 and 20)
findings.evidence: phase doc:328 says "**Test execution output:** 26 new tests. `cargo test -p clio-retrieve --locked` → 191 passed / 0 failed (crate total; 17 of them new here)". My own runs: `cargo test -p clio-retrieve --locked entities` → `test result: ok. 20 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 171 filtered out`; `cargo test -p clio-mcp --locked read_entities` → 5 passed; `cargo test -p clio-write --locked telemetry_entity` → 1 passed; `cargo test -p clio --locked entities` → 3 passed. 20+5+1+3 = 29. `grep -c '^#\[test\]'` on the five new test files gives 13+7+5+1+3 = 29. The 191 crate total is correct, and 191-20 = 171 pre-existing matches the filtered-out count.
findings.requirement_ref: phase 100680 §8 Test and Verification Strategy / §9 Completion Evidence (phase doc:328)
findings.recommendation: Correct the two counts in phase doc:328 to 29 new tests and 20 new in clio-retrieve. The tests themselves all pass; only the evidence line is wrong.

findings.title: Verification limit (3) claims the dense-populated retrieve variant is exercised in the in-process tests; no new test runs a dense-populated retrieve
findings.evidence: phase doc:332 says "The real-binary run used no embedding sidecar, so the dense arm was off and the retrieved hit came from the lexical leg only; entity projection is leg-independent, but the dense-populated variant is exercised only in the in-process tests." Every new in-process test builds its retriever with `fx::retriever(&store)`, documented as "no embedder/reranker by default" (crates/clio-retrieve/src/fixtures_tests.rs:118), and the MCP tests open state with an empty effective overlay (crates/clio-mcp/src/read_entities_tests.rs:41-48), so no embedder is resolved there either. No new test attaches an embedder or asserts on a hit with a non-null `dense_rank`/`scores.semantic`; the real-binary payload confirms the lexical-only shape (`"semantic": null`, `"dense_candidates": 0`). The production path is leg-independent — `finalize` reads the fetched item (crates/clio-retrieve/src/finalize.rs:127) — so this is an evidence inaccuracy, not a defect.
findings.requirement_ref: phase 100680 §9 Completion Evidence, Verification limits (phase doc:332)
findings.recommendation: Either correct the sentence to say the dense-populated variant is not exercised anywhere in this phase, or add one test that attaches a fake embedder and asserts the same `entities` on a dense-ranked hit.

findings.title: Two new public exports in clio-retrieve have no consumer outside the crate
findings.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/lib.rs:76 adds `pub use entities::{SNAPSHOT_ENTITY_FIELD, snapshot_entities};`. A workspace-wide grep shows `SNAPSHOT_ENTITY_FIELD` is referenced only inside crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs (its definition and the one use inside `snapshot_entities`), and `snapshot_entities` only by crates/clio-retrieve/src/finalize.rs:31 (through `crate::entities::`) and crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities_tests.rs (through `crate::entities::`). No other crate imports either name. The module itself is declared `mod entities;` (crates/clio-retrieve/src/lib.rs:46), so the re-export is the only thing widening the crate's public contract.
findings.requirement_ref: phase 100680 §5 Implementation Freedom (phase doc:206) / rust-best-practices public-API hygiene
findings.recommendation: Make the module and helper `pub(crate)` and drop the `pub use` line unless a downstream crate needs them. If a future phase (entity match) needs the projection in `clio-lib` or `clio-mcp`, re-export it then, when there is a real consumer.

findings.title: Definition-of-Done checkbox "Required approval is obtained" is ticked before the approval steps have run
findings.evidence: phase doc:322 reads `- [x] Required approval is obtained (downstream pipeline step: adversary, remediator, remedy approver, finalize).` At the time of this review the only completed step is the developer's (runs/phase-100680/ledger.json lists `developer` alone, routed_to `adversary`), so no approval exists yet. The checkbox is the one DoD item whose truth depends on steps that have not happened.
findings.recommendation: Leave that box unchecked until the remedy approver and finalize steps complete, or reword it as a pipeline-owned item that the developer does not self-certify.

plan_unlimited: Close the telemetry boundary properly: decide the rule with the requirement owner, then add a real leak test that fails when a name reaches a disallowed surface. The current MCP sweep (remove `entities` from every hit, then search the rest of the payload for the probe) is the right shape; the telemetry test should reuse it over the serialized event instead of matching a key name.

Make the span-verification provenance explicit rather than implicit. Carry a flag or a verified-fields record on the stored snapshot so the read side can tell a `store`-verified `entity` from an import-restored or operator-corrected one, and have `snapshot_entities` document the distinction. That turns F-02 from a documentation caveat into a checkable invariant and gives the later entity-match phase a trustworthy signal.

Cover the write paths that skip FR-4 today (bundle import at crates/clio-compliance/src/import_apply.rs, `correct_item`/`update_memory_item`). Either run `verify_snapshot` there or add an explicit `provenance: unverified` marker on the snapshot so no read surface can present the value as span-verified.

Add the missing dense-leg coverage: one test with a fake embedder that asserts `entities` on a dense-ranked hit and that `scores.semantic` is non-null, so the leg-independence claim is executed rather than asserted.

Strengthen the phase's own test inventory: add a test that a bare `RetrieveHit` serialization carries no `entities` key (structural proof the frozen contract is untouched, not just field-value checks), and a test that the key survives a `#[serde(default)]` round trip if `ScoredHit` ever gains a Deserialize derive.

Add a conformance-level check that a dense+lexical mixed hit set still yields identical `entities` across the stdio and Streamable HTTP transports, extending the existing volatile-mask parity test so the always-present key is part of transport parity rather than only of the lexical-only fixture.

Re-audit the PII boundary across every surface that serializes a `RetrieveOutcome` or a `ScoredHit` after future phases land: rerank provider payloads (crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank.rs), the export bundle, hygiene and audit logs, and any new ops report. The phase did this by inspection; a single reusable boundary helper plus a test that calls it from each surface would keep it honest as the surface count grows.
